items.stem: What problem does SD-WAN primarily address compared with traditional MPLS-only WANs?

options.text: Rigid, costly transport and no application-aware path selection
options.rationale: Correct: SD-WAN adds transport flexibility and application-aware routing.

options.text: The need for any physical connectivity at all
options.rationale: SD-WAN still relies on underlying transports.
SD-WAN does not remove IP addressing.

options.text: The need for any security controls
options.rationale: SD-WAN increases, not removes, the need for security.

items.explanation: Correct: SD-WAN adds transport flexibility and application-aware routing.

items.stem: Which TWO are characteristics of SD-WAN architecture? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Separation of the control plane from the data plane
options.rationale: Correct: centralised control is decoupled from forwarding.

options.text: An overlay that runs over multiple transport types
options.rationale: Correct: SD-WAN overlays tunnels across mixed transports.

options.text: A single fixed MPLS circuit per site only

options.rationale: Centralised orchestration is a core feature.

items.stem: Why is application-aware routing valuable in SD-WAN?

options.text: It steers each application over the best-performing available path
options.rationale: Correct: policies match traffic to the path that meets its needs.

options.text: It forces all traffic onto one link regardless of quality
options.rationale: That defeats the purpose of path selection.

options.text: It disables monitoring of link quality
options.rationale: It depends on monitoring link quality.

options.text: It removes the need for any policy
options.rationale: It is driven by application policies.

items.explanation: Correct: policies match traffic to the path that meets its needs.
